problems.title: The unsigned angle score does not by itself identify a convex ear
problems.source_location: Section 3.3, Hole Filling, Eq. (8), PDF p. 6.
claim: Section 3.3, Hole filling, PDF p. 6, Eq. (8), specifies the score
\[ A_i=\operatorname{atan2}\!\left( \|d_{i-1\to i}\times d_{i\to i+1}\|_2, -d_{i-1\to i}\cdot d_{i\to i+1}\right). \]
analysis: The counterclockwise polygon with vertices \[(0,0),(10,0),(10,10),(5.5,10),(5,1),(4.5,10),(0,10)\] has a narrow reflex notch. The cross-product norm removes the orientation sign, so a reflex vertex can receive the smallest unsigned angle even though the proposed ear lies outside the polygon. Uniform scaling preserves the counterexample, including for small holes.

At the notch vertex \((5,1)\), incoming and outgoing vectors \((-0.5,-9)\) and \((-0.5,9)\) have signed cross product \(-9\) and negative dot product \(-80.75\). Its unique minimum score is \(\operatorname{atan2}(9,80.75)\approx6.35966^\circ\), while the triangle centroid \((5,7)\) lies in the excluded notch. The written unrestricted selection therefore chooses an exterior triangle. An implicit standard ear-admissibility guard would reject it, so this does not prove a defect in unavailable code.
result: The unrestricted written angle rule fails on a simple planar boundary. Whether the actual hole-filling implementation already applies a valid-ear guard remains unresolved.
repair: Restrict candidate ears using a planar convexity and interior-admissibility test before ranking their angles. This local proposal does not establish a triangulation guarantee for arbitrary nonplanar boundaries.
A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The defect is in the unrestricted local triangulation specification; an implicit standard ear guard could resolve it, and affected benchmark meshes have not been identified.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: The reported remeshing results do not establish dominance on every metric
claim: Section 4.2, PDF p. 7, describes Table 1 as superiority across every dataset and metric. Table 1 marks Absolute Normal Consistency as a quantity to maximize.
analysis: Table 1 reports Objaverse Absolute Normal Consistency \(75.77\) for Dora and \(75.35\) for Sparc3D at resolution \(512\); at resolution \(1024\), the corresponding entries are \(75.04\) and \(74.98\). Since the metric is maximized, both comparisons contradict dominance on every dataset/metric. The table also supports improvements on other metrics and datasets; no significance or practical-importance claim is made for these small deficits.
result: Supported wording correction bounded to the displayed comparisons.
repair: State that Chamfer distance and F1 improve on all tested datasets, while Objaverse normal consistency is slightly lower than Dora at both matched resolutions.
problems.impact_rationale: Two displayed normal-consistency deficits refute universal all-metric dominance while preserving the favorable results on the other metrics.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

impact_rationale: The literal hole-filling selection rule lacks an admissible-ear condition, and the all-metric sentence overstates its own remeshing table; no failure of the sparse representation or trained models is established.
